newsitem.title: FINLAND: SOCCER-NORWAY GO FOR EXPERIENCE AGAINST FINNS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NORWAY GO FOR EXPERIENCE AGAINST FINNS.

text.p: Norway coach Egil Olsen has recalled experienced duo Gunnar Halle and Jostein Flo for Wednesday's World Cup qualifier against Finland.
With only three home-based players in the team Olsen is hoping the experienced overseas contingent will be able to overcome the Finns and strengthen the Norwegians' grip on group three.
They currently head the standings with 11 points, four clear of Finland and Hungary, all from five games. Switzerland, who visit Oslo in September, have six points with a game in hand.
Norway needed a late equaliser by Ole Gunnar Solskjaer to scrape a 1-1 draw against the Finns in Oslo in April and another draw would not be a disaster for the group leaders.
The Manchester United player was injured in a pre-season club friendly and misses the match.
"It's difficult to play against a team set on defending," said Olsen. "I will not be that happy with a draw, but in the end it might not be that bad," he said.
Olsen's only injury worries concern Erik Mykland and Kjetil Rekdal but both are expected to be fit.

Norway - Frode Grodas (Chelsea), Gunnar Halle (Leeds), Henning Berg (Manchester United), Ronny Johnsen (Manchester United), Stig Inge Bjornebye (Liverpool), Petter Rudi (Molde), Erik Mykland (Panathinaikos), Kjetil Rekdal (Hertha Berlin), Stale Solbakken (Lillestrom), Jostein Flo (Stromsgodset), Tore Andre Flo (Chelsea).
